interpretation.optimization: Enemy sprite mirroring cache tested in a separate diagnostic only. Both full fractional-scale approaches failed exact parity at scale2.3, so neither was applied to app source.

comparison: Preserved pre-cache image transform versus current conservative mirror cache. Rest of Renderer is identical; both paths include identical diagnostic phase markers.

trace.alignment: UserTiming marker in the same renderer main thread maps monotonic trace times to performance.now; sub-millisecond marker-call uncertainty applies.

scene: 1500 moving enemies + six actual weapon behaviors, Amount12/Cooldown0.3/Duration2/Area1.1,400XP,600pooledparticles. Invincible,1e9enemyHP; no entity reduction.
limitations: Diagnostic phase markers and tracing add overhead; these results are attribution evidence, not a performance gate.
Two real-time Chromium play sessions share the cloud instance; scheduling/raster-backend stalls remain possible.
Phase boundaries include JavaScript plus time blocked in canvas submission. A long canvas call alone does not distinguish scheduler preemption from backend synchronization.
Source application files were not edited; instrumentation exists only in the diagnostic esbuild bundle.

optimizationEvidence.scope: Only mirrored sprites at exact scales1,1.2,2; all other scales retain original transform. Cache bounded128entries.
optimizationEvidence.comparisonCaveat: Sequential runs with tracing and phase markers; reduced times are observations in this run, not an isolated causal percentage or target-Windows guarantee.
